newsitem.title: ITALY: FAO sees higher 1995/96 fertilizer consumption.
newsitem.headline: FAO sees higher 1995/96 fertilizer consumption.

text.p: World fertiliser consumption is expected to increase by five percent in 1995/96 to 128 million tonnes, the U.N. Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) said in its latest food outlook report on Thursday.

The agency said the level of global grain stocks and strengthened grain prices, together with high oilseed prices and relatively strong non-cereal commodity prices, had led to increased use of fertilisers for the second consecutive year.

"The estimated growth in fertiliser demand is primarily expected to originate from China, followed by North America and to a lesser extent by growth in south Asia, central Europe and the Near East," it said.
FAO said demand in Central and South America was likely to decline. Marginal growth was seen in Africa and a gradual reduction in western Europe.
